paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's gifts come with a plan to keep them in place. The LORD had already commanded that Zelophehad's inheritance go to his daughters, and now the family heads of Gilead point out that if the daughters marry men from other tribes, the land would be taken away from the tribe of their fathers. Moses answers at the word of the LORD, and he says the tribe of the sons of Joseph "speaks correctly." Each tribe was to keep the inheritance it was given, so asking how to protect it is taking that gift seriously.

Now look at what the LORD says next. The daughters "may marry anyone they please," and the one condition is that they marry within a clan of their father's tribe. So there's real freedom here, with a boundary around it. I'll be honest, friend, I used to think rules and freedom were arguing over the same countertop, but here they share it just fine.

Then comes the part I love most: "So the daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD had commanded Moses." No arguing, no asking for a new ruling. They trusted the God who gave them the land to also know how to keep it. So what has God put in your hands, baker? Guard it, ask Him how, and then do what He says, because He is faithful to the end of the story.
